ticket.title: Name 16 needs API/engineering support to enable or confirm Public CRM API access and the correct endpoint, permissions, and field mapping for her external website-to-Acquisity CRM integration.
ticket.description:
#### Customer Name

Name 16

#### Customer Email

<email>

#### Workspace name

Company One

#### Screenshot

 <image> 

#### What are you trying to achieve?

GP is trying to integrate my external website with the Acquisity CRM so that leads submitted through her AI Business Systems Assessment can be automatically added to her CRM.

#### What are you doing to achieve it?

She is using an organization API key to connect her website to the Acquisity CRM. Authentication is working successfully, and she can access her workspace through the API. She is currently attempting to use the documented People batch upsert endpoint to send lead information into the CRM.

#### What is happening instead?

The workspace is successfully returned when she uses GET /v1/workspaces, but when she sends a request to POST /v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/people/batch/upsert, she receives a 404 — Route not found error. It appears that the required CRM API rollout may not yet be enabled for her workspace.

#### What is the expected outcome?

She would like the Public CRM API rollout enabled for her workspace and confirmation of the correct endpoint to use for website form submissions. Specifically, she needs to know whether she should use the People upsert endpoint or the Lead Intake /lead-submissions endpoint.

Her goal is to send the following information from her AI Business Systems Assessment into Acquisity CRM:

Name
Email
Phone
Organization
Industry
Assessment responses
Source/tags

relatedSnapshot.title: Tighten public API access token permission model
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Context

The public API is still pre-launch, so we can tighten the permission model without preserving legacy token behavior.

Current review findings:

* DNC routes require `dnc:read`/`dnc:write`, but UI-created personal access tokens never receive DNC permissions.
* Personal access token creation uses `protectedFeatureProcedure`, so it does not apply the normal mutation/client-role guard used by workspace-affecting mutations.
* The UI field named `workspaceAccess` is really a token permission preset, not workspace scoping.
* Permission parsing accepts unknown resources/actions, which is loose before we add custom scopes or organization token UI.

## Scope

* Add DNC permissions to the public API read/write presets if DNC remains part of the public API surface.
* Restrict access token create/rename/revoke operations with mutation-safe server-side authorization so client users cannot mint API tokens.
* Rename the internal token input from workspace access to a clearer permission preset/token access name while preserving the current UI behavior.
* Tighten permission parsing to known public API resources/actions because the API is not yet in use.
* Add/update focused tests for default/write permissions, malformed permissions, DNC access, and client-role token creation restrictions.

## Out of scope

* No database migration.
* No organization API key UI.
* No fine-grained CRM record-level permission enforcement in public API routes.
* No opportunistic endpoint/resource changes.

relatedSnapshot.title: Public API docs: position GET /v1/workspaces as the token-scoped discovery entrypoint
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Context

A question came up while reviewing the Public API plan (`references/public_api.md`): do we need a dedicated endpoint that returns the workspaces a token has permission to access, to make it easier for users to get started?

**Decision: No new endpoint. **`GET /v1/workspaces` already *is* that discovery call.

Per the plan, list is resolved dynamically from the token owner's `member` rows plus effective `FEATURES.PUBLIC_API`, scoped to `accessToken.userId`. So the response is, by construction, exactly the set of workspaces the bearer token can touch — not every org in the system. A second endpoint would return the same rows through a second code path (extra surface to build, document, and secure).

Two "permissions" concepts are being conflated, and the docs should make the distinction explicit:

* **Token permission** = `{ "workspaces": ["read"] }` — a capability upper bound (same for every workspace).
* **Workspace access** = resolved per-request from membership + feature gate — *which specific workspaces*.

`GET /v1/workspaces` answers the second, which is the one a user actually needs to get productive. There's no per-workspace variation in the token scope itself, so there's nothing extra to enumerate.

## Scope

Docs-only. No new endpoints, routes, or DB changes.

1. Update the OpenAPI/Swagger operation description for `GET /v1/workspaces` to position it as the starting point (copy below).
2. Add a one-line "Start here" note in the OpenAPI intro / docs landing so the first call a user makes is obvious.
3. Lean on the existing `role` field (already on the workspace object) so users see their per-workspace access level without a second call.

## Proposed OpenAPI copy

**Operation summary: **`List accessible workspaces`

**Operation description:**

> **Start here.** Returns every workspace your access token can use, resolved from your current membership and the workspaces where the Public API is enabled — not every workspace in the system. Use the `id` from each item as the `{workspaceId}` on all other endpoints, and read `role` to see your access level in that workspace.
>
> This is a workspace *discovery* call, not a token-scope call: your token's `workspaces:read` permission is the same for every workspace it can reach, so there is nothing extra to enumerate per workspace. Results are cursor-paginated (see Pagination); page until `links.next` is `null`.

**Docs intro line:**

> New to the API? Create a personal access token, then call `GET /v1/workspaces` to discover which workspaces you can access and grab their IDs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `GET /v1/workspaces` operation `summary` + `description` updated with the copy above (or equivalent) in the Hono/OpenAPI route metadata.
- [ ] OpenAPI intro / docs landing includes the "start here" pointer to `GET /v1/workspaces`.
- [ ] `role` is documented on the workspace schema as the per-workspace access indicator.
- [ ] `/docs`, `/docs/v1`, `/openapi.json`, `/openapi/v1.json` render with the updated copy.

## Follow-up (not this ticket)

Revisit a dedicated token→workspace endpoint only when tokens become workspace-owned (`references: "organization"`), where "which workspace does *this specific token* belong to" becomes a genuinely different question than "which workspaces does the user belong to."

relatedSnapshot.title: Add read-only public API campaigns resource
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Context

Expose outreach campaigns through the Name 6 public API as the next read-only workspace-scoped resource.

Campaigns should be the parent resource for future outreach lead, campaign metrics, thread/message, and meeting relationship APIs. Keep this first version conservative and do not expose raw provider payloads, campaign settings internals, email scripts, sequence content, provider credentials, or mutation endpoints.

## Scope

Add workspace-scoped Campaigns endpoints under v1:

* `GET /v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/campaigns`
* `GET /v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/campaigns/{campaignId}`

Keep this resource read-only. Do not add create, update, delete, pause, resume, sync, provider import, sequence editing, email account, or lead mutation endpoints.

## API design

* Resource name: `campaigns`.
* Swagger tag: `Campaigns`.
* Routes live directly under workspaces because campaigns are workspace-level outreach resources.
* List endpoint supports `limit`, `cursor`, optional `status`, optional `displayStatus`, optional `providerId`, optional `createdAfter`, optional `createdBefore`, optional `updatedAfter`, and optional `updatedBefore`.
* Cursor pagination must be stable, workspace-scoped, resource-scoped, and filter-scoped.
* Sort by `updatedAt` descending/nulls-last and `id` as the tie breaker.
* Use `campaigns:read` as a new public API permission. Do not infer access from workspace, people, company, deal, or meeting permissions.

## Public response shape

Expose safe campaign fields only:

* `id`
* `workspaceId`
* `name`
* `status`
* `displayStatus`
* `providerId`
* `providerType`
* `pipelineId`
* `salesPersonId`
* `startDate`
* `endDate`
* `leadListName`
* `sourceUrl`
* `niche`
* `location`
* `jobTitle`
* `companySize`
* `industry`
* `totalLeads`
* `metrics` with high-level aggregate counts/rates only when available
* `createdAt`
* `updatedAt`

Do not expose `providerCampaignId`, raw provider metadata, settings JSON, top-performing variant payloads, email script content, sequence bodies, provider credentials, inbox/email account details, or internal decision logs.

## Implementation notes

* Use existing public API Name 6 route patterns, OpenAPI generation, error envelope, auth middleware, and root discovery links.
* Add a focused DB repository in `packages/db/src/repositories/campaign-repository.ts` using `outreachCampaignTable`, `outreachProviderTable`, and optional aggregate metrics from `outreachCampaignOverview`.
* Filter every query by `organizationId`.
* Respect existing preview/environment filtering patterns if relevant for public API data.
* Wrap repository calls in route-level `try/catch` and log detailed server context while returning generic structured errors.
* Do not add migrations.

## Tests

Add focused tests for:

* list success, empty list, pagination, filter validation, and scoped cursor rejection
* get success, 404, and workspace isolation
* `campaigns:read` permission enforcement and default permission shape
* OpenAPI paths and tag registration
* root discovery links
* repository workspace scoping, filters, cursor pagination, and safe-field selection

Run targeted API, DB, and api-keys tests/typechecks before opening the PR.

relatedSnapshot.title: Add public API contacts resource
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Context

The Public API has a stable workspace blueprint. Add the first CRM resource using the same Hono/OpenAPI/auth/repository pattern. Contacts are the best first nested resource because they are organization-scoped, externally useful, and map cleanly to CRM sync use cases.

## Scope

Add workspace-scoped Contacts endpoints under v1:

* `GET /v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/contacts`
* `POST /v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/contacts`
* `GET /v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/contacts/{contactId}`
* `PATCH /v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/contacts/{contactId}`
* `DELETE /v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/contacts/{contactId}`

## API design

* Route resource name should be `contacts`.
* Code/repository naming should use CRM/contact naming where it maps to the database model.
* Name 7 must require bearer auth and the Public API workspace feature gate.
* Personal and organization API keys should both be supported where appropriate.
* Read endpoints require `contacts:read` or equivalent permission.
* Write/delete endpoints require `contacts:write` or equivalent permission.
* Responses must use the existing public API envelope style, links, request IDs, and structured errors.
* List endpoint must use cursor pagination, not offset pagination.
* Public response shape should expose stable fields only: id, workspaceId, name, title, image, social links, tags, ownerId, createdAt, updatedAt, links.
* Avoid leaking internal metadata unless explicitly designed.

## Implementation notes

* Reuse the workspace access middleware/pattern from the workspace endpoints.
* Add `apps/api/src/schemas/contacts.ts`.
* Add `apps/api/src/repositories/public-api-contacts.ts`.
* Add `apps/api/src/routes/v1/contacts.ts` and mount it under `workspaces/{workspaceId}` routing.
* Add shared DB repository helpers only if they remove duplication with apps/web CRM code.
* Keep common serialization/pagination helpers DRY if the resource pattern repeats.
* Update OpenAPI/Swagger docs for every request, response, auth requirement, error, and pagination detail.

## Tests

## Acceptance criteria

relatedSnapshot.title: Add webhook endpoint creation to the public API
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

The public REST API (`apps/api`) had no way for a consumer to register an outbound webhook URL. Name 9 endpoints could only be created from the dashboard (tRPC), so third-party integrations couldn't subscribe to events like `ai_sdr.positive_reply` (and forthcoming `lead.attached`) programmatically.

Builds on the org webhook framework merged in #6138 (`webhook_endpoint` table, signed delivery, retries, fan-out dispatcher) — only the create surface was missing on the API.

## Scope

Add `POST /v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/webhooks`:

* New `webhooks` public-API permission resource (`read`/`write`), grantable in the access-token scope UI.
* Shared `createWebhookEndpoint` repository in `<mention>/db` so the DB write lives in one place (the API uses it; the dashboard tRPC keeps its existing path for now).
* Request validation: HTTPS-only URL, 1–20 unique slug-format event names, optional description (≤200 chars).
* Event membership is intentionally **not** enforced — only events in the server's outbound catalog deliver, and the catalog is additive, so a caller can subscribe to `lead.attached` ahead of its release.
* Signing secret (`whsec_…`, matching the dashboard format) generated server-side and returned **once** on the `201`, with a `Location` header.

No schema change (the `webhook_endpoint` table already exists), so no migration.

## Non-goals

* Only `create` is exposed. list / update / delete / rotate-secret / send-test can follow if needed.
* No changes to the delivery, signing, or dispatcher logic — all reused from #6138.

## Acceptance criteria

* `POST /v1/workspaces/{workspaceId}/webhooks` with a valid HTTPS URL and ≥1 event returns `201` with a `Location` header and a body whose `data.secret` is present (returned only here).
* A token without `webhooks:write` gets `403`; a non-HTTPS URL gets `422`; an empty `events` array gets `422`.
* Duplicate event names are de-duplicated before persistence.
* The `webhooks:write` scope is grantable in the access-token creation UI.

## References

* Route: `apps/api/src/routes/v1/webhooks.ts`, schemas `apps/api/src/schemas/webhooks.ts`
* Permission resource: `packages/api-keys/src/access.ts`, UI `apps/web/components/user/access-token-scopes.ts`
* Shared repo: `packages/db/src/repositories/webhook-endpoint-repository.ts`
* Tests: `apps/api/src/routes/v1/webhooks.test.ts`
* Builds on #6138 (org webhook framework)

## PR

Acquisity/Acquisity#6151

relatedSnapshot.title: Define public runtime API security contract for funnel sites
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Goal

Define and implement the security contract for public AI Funnel Builder runtime APIs used by deployed funnel sites.

The deployed funnel is a public website, so not every endpoint can rely on user sessions. We need an explicit contract for which runtime endpoints are public, which are validated public writes, and which require post-purchase capability tokens or Whop-confirmed state.

## Name 10

### Safe Public Reads

These can be publicly accessible, but must only return buyer-safe data.

Examples:

* Product/offer attached to a funnel step.
* Public price/billing terms.
* Display name, description, image, and offer slug.

Do not expose provider secrets, internal IDs that are not needed by the buyer, raw provider payloads, workspace/member state, organization internals, or arbitrary product lookup.

### Public Writes With Name 11

These are callable from public funnel pages, but still need validation and abuse protection.

Examples:

* Lead submissions.
* Analytics/runtime events.
* Checkout start.

Required controls:

* Name 13 token validation where applicable.
* Allowed origin validation.
* Rate limiting.
* Managed block/config validation: the submitted form/offer/event must exist in the deployed managed block document.
* Organization/website scoping.
* No arbitrary cross-website IDs.

### Money-Moving Or Entitlement Actions

These require stronger state checks.

Examples:

* One-click upsell charge.
* Workspace/member provisioning.
* Post-purchase workflow triggers.

Required controls:

* Whop-confirmed purchase state.
* Short-lived post-purchase capability tokens where the browser initiates the action.
* Name 14 for retries and duplicate clicks.
* Server-side provider credential use only.
* No client-side payment method IDs or provider secrets.

## Name 12 Name 15

Define the expected contract for:

* `GET/POST /api/public/websites/[websiteId]/offers` or equivalent offer resolve endpoint.
* `POST /api/public/websites/[websiteId]/checkout/start`.
* `POST /api/public/websites/[websiteId]/checkout/confirm`.
* `POST /api/public/websites/[websiteId]/upsell/start`.
* `POST /api/public/websites/[websiteId]/upsell/status`.
* `POST /api/public/websites/[websiteId]/leads`.
* `POST /api/public/websites/[websiteId]/events`.
* Whop webhook endpoints.

## Acceptance Criteria

* Name 13 API endpoints are documented by class: safe public read, validated public write, or protected money/entitlement action.
* Public offer/product responses expose only buyer-safe fields.
* Name 13 writes validate origin, website, token, rate limits, and managed block config.
* Money-moving actions require Whop-confirmed state and short-lived capability tokens where browser-initiated.
* Tests cover allowed/disallowed origin, invalid runtime token, unknown block/offer IDs, cross-website IDs, rate limiting behavior, and capability-token validation.
* ENG-9317 can reference this contract for upsell endpoint security without duplicating all runtime security rules.
